text.title: 指向别处的链接
text.situation:
一位读者发来截图，声称整座图书馆会关闭。它的设计几乎与正式通知无法区分，链接却通往陌生页面。诺拉要先核查真实性，再判断是不是骗局。她们对照原文件，向图书馆办公室询问来源。回复表明，有人复制旧通知，并编造了新日期。乔把模糊笔记改成对差别的事实说明。故事吸引人，是因为它能抓住注意；证据令人信服，则是因为它支持了更正。她们无需把错误故事说得更可怕，也能说明它为何不对。

乔：两个设计几乎分不出来。
诺拉：检查链接和日期。
乔：办公室已确认截图是骗局。
诺拉：那就按事实说明改动在哪里。

paragraphs.en: A reader sent Jo a screenshot claiming the whole library would close. Its design was almost indistinguishable from the official notice, but the link led to an unfamiliar page. Nora would not call it a hoax until they had checked its authenticity. They compared the screenshot with the original file and asked the library office where it had come from. The reply showed that someone had copied an old notice and invented a new date. Jo replaced her vague note with a factual account of the difference. The story was compelling enough to hold attention; the evidence was compelling for a different reason, because it supported the correction. They did not need to make the false story more frightening to explain why it was wrong.

paragraphs.en:
Jo: The two designs are nearly indistinguishable.
Nora: Check the link and the date.
Jo: The office has confirmed that the screenshot is a hoax.
Nora: Then give readers a factual explanation of what changed.

S16.N10.P01.function: A link that led somewhere else
acceptableAnswers: 乔根据事实说明了差别。 诺拉核查通知的真实性。 截图原来是一场骗局。

S16.N10.P02.function: A link that led somewhere else
acceptableAnswers: 复制设计与原版几乎无法区分。 乔用准确说明替换模糊笔记。

S16.N10.P03.function: A link that led somewhere else
S16.N10.P03.cue: 说明故事为何吸引人、证据为何令人信服。
acceptableAnswers: 故事足够引人入胜，能抓住注意。 原文件提供了令人信服的证据。

S16.N10.T01.function: A link that led somewhere else
S16.N10.T01.cue: 两个副本看起来一样，描述区分的困难。
acceptableAnswers: 这些副本几乎无法区分。
